What

What Fallen Tree Removal Involves

Fallen tree removal is the extraction of a tree that has already failed — down on the ground, resting on a structure, or across a driveway, fence, or vehicle. Unlike a planned removal, there is no felling decision to make; the job is safely freeing the tree from whatever it landed on, protecting the property from further damage, and hauling everything away. When a covered structure is involved, Roubic builds the insurance documentation package before any cutting begins.

The distinction that matters: a fallen tree is an unstable load. Trunks under tension, root plates still attached, and limbs pinned against a roof all release energy when cut in the wrong order. Aaron and the crew read the load first, tarp any roof opening, rig with crane support when the weight demands it, and dismantle in a controlled sequence rather than just cutting where it's easiest.

Why

Four Reasons Homeowners Call Roubic

The fallen-tree scenarios Aaron's crew handles most often across NE Ohio.

Tree on the House or Garage

A tree through the roof after a high-wind night. Crane support, roof tarp, and full scene documentation for the insurance claim.

Driveway or Road Blocked

Tree Across a Fence or Line

Vehicle or Structure Damage

Common Fallen-Tree Questions

Fallen Tree Removal FAQ

Five things NE Ohio homeowners want to know after a tree comes down.

What do I do if a tree falls on my house?
Call {{global.phone}} right away. We dispatch with crane support, photograph the scene for your insurance, tarp any roof opening, and coordinate full extraction. Stay out of the damaged area until the crew arrives — a pinned tree is under tension and limbs can shift without warning.
Will my insurance pay for fallen tree removal?
Usually yes when the tree has damaged a covered structure — house, garage, fence, or a vehicle in covered scenarios. Removing a standing tree that hasn't hit anything is a homeowner expense. Roubic's documentation package (scene photos, itemized scope, species and DBH estimates, before/after photos) is built to meet carrier requirements on first submission.
How fast can Roubic respond to a fallen tree?
Our target on-site window in Tier 1 and Tier 2 markets is 2–4 hours, conditions permitting. Tier 3 markets are typically 3–5 hours. Active high winds or lightning delay dispatch until it's safe for the crew to work.
What if the fallen tree is across a power line?
Stay clear of the whole area and report the downed line to FirstEnergy / The Illuminating Company first. Roubic coordinates with the utility on power-line-adjacent extraction, but we never work in direct contact with energized lines — the utility clears the wire portion before we handle the tree.
Do you haul away all the debris?
Yes. A standard fallen-tree job includes full debris haul-off with our Bandit chipper — nothing left in your driveway or yard. If you want the wood cut to firewood lengths and stacked instead, just say so; there's no price difference either way.
